src/application/PlaceOrderUseCase.ts: the constructor takes the domain ports OrderRepository, StockReservationService and IdGenerator; it has no concrete persistence or transport code

src/application/PlaceOrderUseCase.ts: `if (typeof command.customerId !== "string" || command.customerId === "")` is an input guard on the command, which is acceptable in the application layer (borderline)
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The file does what an application-layer use case should do: it coordinates the work and leaves the business rules to the domain. PlaceOrderUseCase.execute checks the incoming command and builds the domain objects (OrderLine.create, new Order). It then calls the domain stock service (stock.reserve) and the domain repository port (orders.save), and converts the result to an application DTO (toOrderDto).

There is no persistence, transport or framework code here. Its dependencies are domain abstractions passed in through the constructor. Quantity and line rules sit in OrderLine.create and Order, not in this file.

One check is borderline: the customerId test (non-empty string) throws a DomainError. You could argue the rule "an order needs a customer" belongs in the Order constructor. But a guard on the input command's shape is a normal application-layer job, so I don't count it as misplaced business logic.
